This map clarifies the continuous distance gradient along the left wall, floor, and recessed ceiling and cleanly separates the 3-to-5-metre background person and sofa from the sub-1.5-metre foreground furniture more distinctly than RGB alone, though it is unreliable on the wall clock (which vanishes into the flat wall plane) and inside the open shelving cubbies where depth boundaries blur.
segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete objects in the room across the 5-frame leftward pan, consistently detecting the television screen (0.5 to 1 metre ahead and within reach), the potted plant resting on the top-right corner of the right shelf (about 1 to 1.5 metres away and slightly above the TV), the circular clock mounted on the wall above the TV (except in frames 3 and 5), and the low table on the left at 3 to 5 metres and out of reach. In frame 5, as the camera turns left, it segments the partially visible person in blue and the adjacent background hand/arm in the bottom-left corner at 3 to 5 metres (out of arm's reach of the camera wearer and each other), where the background masks overlap and partially occlude the green table mask behind them. While segmentation provides crisp 2D object boundaries for the TV, plant, and table that separate them from cluttered surroundings, it is highly unreliable for semantic and spatial scene understanding here. It completely misses the shelving units, floor toys, ottoman, and sofa, inconsistently labels the left-side coffee table as a 'bed' in frame 1, 'dining table' in frames 2, 4, and 5, and omits it in frame 3, and misclassifies the bowl of fruit on that table as 'pizza' in frame 4. Furthermore, it falsely segments 2D cartoon characters and an eagle displayed on the flat TV screen (0.5 to 1 metre away and within reach) as real 'person' instances in frames 2 through 5, creating false-positive subjects that appear to face away from the room.
pose: The body/hand skeleton map is completely blank across frames 1 to 4, confirming that no real people are visible in the room during the initial stationary view toward the television and shelves 0.5 to 1.5 metres away and within reach. In frame 5, as the camera wearer turns leftward, a single yellow upper-body/arm skeletal segment appears in the bottom-left corner, corresponding to the person in a blue shirt positioned 3 to 5 metres away and out of arm's reach of the camera wearer and roughly 3 to 5 metres in front of the coffee table. The diagonal orientation of this skeletal link from the left edge down toward the lower-left indicates the person's torso and arm are angled rightward across the lower background rather than facing squarely away from the camera, with most of their body and head cropped out of the left frame boundary. Unlike the segmentation map, the pose estimator usefully filters out the 2D cartoon figures on the TV screen 0.5 to 1 metre away and isolates only the real background person in frame 5. However, the map is largely unreliable in frame 5 because heavy edge truncation and long distance cause it to miss the person's full torso and head orientation, and it completely fails to render a magenta hand skeleton for the open hand clearly visible out of arm's reach at the bottom-left next to the person.
